Hildegard 0.1.15 is a pre-alpha. It adds short one-time codes for joining a device and for approving a chatbot.

## Install

- **macOS and Linux:** `curl -fsSL https://dbaney.com/hildegard/install.sh | sh`
- **Windows (PowerShell):** `irm https://dbaney.com/hildegard/install.ps1 | iex`
- **Desktop app:** pick your system's download below, or from [dbaney.com/hildegard](https://dbaney.com/hildegard/).

Installed already? Hildegard updates itself, or run `hildegard update` (or `hildegard update all` for every device).

## New

- **Join a device with a short code.** `hildegard choir invite` and Settings › Devices › Share this GPU now show a
  code like `HG-7QX2-M9KD` with the one command to run on the other device:
  `hildegard choir join HG-7QX2-M9KD --url <address>`. A code works once, for 10 minutes. The code goes only to the
  address you give, never to other devices on your tailnet. The long `hgc1_` code is still available
  (`hildegard choir invite --long`, or Show long code).
- **Approve a chatbot with a code.** An owner can make a one-time connect code with `hildegard host code` or Settings ›
  Sharing › Get a connect code. On Hildegard's approval page, choose Use a connect code and type it instead of your
  name and passphrase. Only type a code you made yourself for this connection.
- Wrong codes are limited: 5 per source and 60 across all sources in 15 minutes. After that, no code works until the
  window passes, but a passphrase or a long code still does. A new passphrase drops that owner's unused codes.

## Under the hood

- Each device now reports what it can do (microphone, speaker, speech and language models, GPU) to the devices it
  shares with. This lays the groundwork for Talk.
